baseline.reason: Verified via run_poc with the identical /poc/run.sh across all three revisions (same command, same input). pre_intro: exit=0, no TSAN report — expected because src/networking.c in pre_intro has no `c->iolookedcmd = lookupCommand(c->argv, c->argc)` call from the I/O thread (confirmed absent by source diff). post_intro: exit=66, TSAN fired reliably (2 extra confirmation runs outside run_poc also hit it) with report "ThreadSanitizer: data race /work/src/dict.c:1073 in dictNext", where the racing read is `dictFind (dict.c:808) <- dictFetchValue <- lookupSubcommand <- lookupCommandLogic <- lookupCommand <- processInputBuffer (networking.c:2781) <- readQueryFromClient <- IOThreadMain` (i.e. an I/O thread reading dict->useStoredKeyApi during a command lookup) racing against the main thread's dictNext() safe-iterator pause/resume-rehash bookkeeping (dict->pauserehash) on the same dict object — exactly the hazard described in the fix commit message ("main thread modifies pauserehash in dictNext while IO thread reads useStoredKeyApi() in lookupCommand()->dictFind() path"). This matches the intro commit's structural change (PR #13696 offloading lookupCommand to I/O threads) combined with the pre-existing bitfield-packing hazard in struct dict (pauserehash/useStoredKeyApi sharing one storage word in both pre_intro and post_intro's dict.h). post_benign: exit=0, no TSAN report, and source diff confirms the fix commit's change is present — dict.h's `pauserehash` is now a full non-shared unsigned word, and `useStoredKeyApi` instead shares a word with `pauseAutoResize` (which the fix message states is never mutated for command dicts), eliminating the concurrent RMW hazard while the racy I/O-thread lookupCommand call path itself remains unchanged/present. This satisfies the crash/no-crash/no-crash pattern required to confirm both bug introduction and the benign fix for this DataRace.
